timing: Exploratory extension after the signed SPIRE beam measurements and optical-neighbour counts, before beam-overlap results.
question: How much do the actual optical separations and measured SPIRE beams limit independent host amplitudes, even before uncertainty about which neighbours emit?
sample: The existing 265 selected eight-band DES hosts with valid measurements in all three SPIRE bands. Exact deep-catalogue host coordinates and distinct galaxy IDs.
candidate_neighbours: All other unflagged optical galaxies of the same DECam deep field, within twice the published approximate SPIRE FWHM. No cut on their unknown infrared flux.
empirical_beams: ESA 1arcsec Neptune beam maps; radially averaged observed beam profile is the primary rotation-independent approximation. Native two-dimensional beam at four position angles is a nearest-pair sensitivity.
nearest_pair: Normalized beam-template correlation rho; conditional independent-white-pixel noise inflation 1/sqrt(1-rho^2). Gaussian analytic comparison at the same nominal FWHM.
all_candidates: Project the host template against all candidate-neighbour templates and a constant/linear sky plane on a finite map-pixel grid. Compare residual template norm with the host-plus-sky-only norm. SVD is rank-revealing; no ridge or positivity prior is imposed.
interpretation: Geometric conditional information, not measured dust fluxes, intrinsic luminosities or a calibrated confidence interval. Optical neighbours need not emit in the infrared; an optical catalogue is not a complete infrared source list. Beam source-spectrum, mapmaking, extension and correlated noise assumptions remain. No new age or cosmological correction is fitted.
